semantic_obligations: The four exact logical inputs must satisfy the C4 DecisionNecessity cross-bindings.
Zero objections may derive QualifiedDecisionNecessity and only that positive fact may authorize mechanical DecisionRequest projection.
Objections do not prove that no product decision is needed; they require the one DiscoveryDecisionRequired revision when current and admissible.
There is no second generic challenge layer above DecisionNecessityChallenge.
At least one atomic classification statement is required.
The classification statement array is ordered semantic value and duplicate exact canonical statements are invalid.
Discovery is routing evidence and does not independently authorize repair, finding refutation, Decision Request, Gate A readiness, or another external outcome.
NotEstablished is forbidden.
The prior DecisionNecessityCandidate Fact is mandatory and is the exact positive closure candidate that received the hostile objections.
The prior DecisionNecessityChallenge must be the exact challenge of the prior DecisionNecessityCandidate and contain one or more objections.
A positive revised statement retains semantic_disposition exactly decision-required, may revise only the exact targeted statement, and must not modify sibling Discovery classifications.
NotEstablished withdraws only that exact decision-required closure and does not establish that no product decision is needed.
A positive revised statement invalidates reuse of the old UniqueCorrectionExhaustion Fact; it enters a fresh ordinary UniqueCorrection path.
No second Discovery decision-required revision exists.
The prior targeted statement must have semantic_disposition exactly no-normative-impact.
The prior NoNormativeImpactChallenge must target the exact prior statement Fact and contain one or more objections.
A positive revised statement retains semantic_disposition exactly no-normative-impact and may revise only the exact targeted statement.
Sibling Discovery statements remain immutable.
NotEstablished withdraws only the positive no-normative-impact claim and does not establish normative impact.
A positive revision requires one fresh NoNormativeImpactChallenge@1 and no second Discovery no-normative-impact revision exists.
The semantic candidate contains exactly the seven protocol-defined materiality axes and one non-empty rationale.
Materiality is mechanically OR(all seven axes); no independent material boolean exists.
The question assumes the finding is true and assesses whether the Gate A subject could remain unchanged while still legitimately authorizing the candidate model.
An all-false candidate requires MaterialityChallenge@1; NotEstablished is forbidden.
The prior MaterialityAssessment must be all-false.
The prior MaterialityChallenge must target the exact prior assessment and contain one or more objections.
The revision answers only those exact objections without branch-switching or free second semantic search.
A positive-axis revision qualifies directly; an all-false revision requires one fresh MaterialityChallenge@1.
NotEstablished is forbidden and no second MaterialityAssessment revision exists.
The challenged MaterialityAssessment must have all seven axes false.
The challenge hostile-tests the exact challenged candidate against every ordered materiality objective and emits every established objection.
Zero objections may derive QualifiedNonMateriality; objections never imply positive materiality.

A challenge to an initial candidate with objections requires the one MaterialityAssessment revision when current and admissible; objections to a revised candidate terminate the non-material closure path.
The targeted Discovery statement must have semantic_disposition exactly no-normative-impact.
Zero objections may derive QualifiedNoNormativeImpact.
Objections do not prove normative impact and require the one DiscoveryNoNormativeImpact revision when current and admissible.
The challenged admission must contain a positive RealizationScopeCandidate.
Candidate binding is inherited through the challenged admission and the challenge must not independently infer or select another candidate.
Zero objections may derive AcceptedRealizationScope.
AcceptedRealizationScope remains bound to the exact CandidateRevision and never transfers by content equality.
CandidateRevision and complete CandidateView are both required and must satisfy CandidateViewOf(C, complete, V).
Distinct CandidateRevision IDs produce distinct RealizationScope QLEKs even when CandidateView values are structurally equal.
A positive candidate contains exact readable_paths, writable_paths, completeness_argument, and minimal_write_authority_argument.
Paths are exact raw candidate-path identities; globs, wildcards, directory prefixes, fuzzy selectors, and mutable-workspace lookups are forbidden.

writable_paths is a subset of readable_paths; every correction requirement has exactly one requirement surface; the union of requirement surface paths equals readable_paths; every writable path has exact necessity justification; controlling product-authority paths are not writable.
The scope is a maximum authorized physical boundary, not a patch; NotEstablished means only that no safe sufficient candidate-bound scope was established.
The prior RealizationScope must be positive and the prior RealizationScopeChallenge must target it and contain one or more objections.
The revision retains the exact same SurvivingMaterialBasis, AcceptedUniqueCorrection, CandidateRevision, and complete CandidateView as the initial producer question.
The revision must not resolve current candidate again or rebase to another candidate.
Candidate staleness before lawful dispatch removes current-progression need but does not change the old QLEK; a lawfully dispatched later completion remains part of that old QLEK history.
A positive revision requires one fresh RealizationScopeChallenge@1 and no second RealizationScope revision exists.
The challenged admission must contain a positive RefutationCandidate.
Zero objections may derive QualifiedRefutation.
Objections to an initial positive candidate require the one Refutation revision when current and admissible.
Objections to a revised positive candidate may establish the revised-challenge-objections RefutationExhaustion branch; no opposite finding-truth proposition is implied.
A positive candidate must invalidate at least one necessary premise or inference of the finding from exact admissible authority/evidence without introducing a new normative assumption.
Refutation grounds are limited to the immutable adjudication-output-v1 RefutationCandidate domain.
Reviewer majority, absence of another finding, author intent, preferred interpretation, difficulty reproducing, and future implementation are not refutation grounds.
NotEstablished means only that this question did not establish a refutation candidate; it never means the finding is true.
The prior Refutation must be a positive RefutationCandidate.
The prior RefutationChallenge must target the exact prior Refutation and contain one or more objections.
The revision answers only those exact objections within the same refutation family.
NotEstablished withdraws the refutation candidate and terminates this bounded refutation path without qualified refutation.
A positive revision requires one fresh RefutationChallenge@1 and no second Refutation revision exists.
The challenged admission must contain a positive RepairRealizationCandidate.
The challenge hostile-tests both already-realized claims and proposed patch realization.
Candidate binding is inherited through the challenged admission.
Zero objections may derive AcceptedRepairRealization and the resulting fact remains bound to the exact CandidateRevision.
The scoped CandidateView coverage kind is readable-paths and its exact path set equals AcceptedRealizationScope.readable_paths for the exact CandidateRevision.
Every exact UniqueCorrection requirement appears exactly once in requirement_realizations and is classified exactly already-realized or patch-realized.
The union of patch-realized operation paths equals the exact set of proposed operation paths and no operation contributes to no requirement.
Every operation supplies one exact raw candidate path and exact desired after-state, and every operation path belongs to AcceptedRealizationScope.writable_paths.

The model does not emit authoritative before-state, trusted preimage, ArtifactRef, diff, patch hunk, search/replace, shell operation, or merge instruction; the runner derives exact before-state from the scoped CandidateView.
No operation may be a physical no-op; operations is empty iff every requirement is already-realized; a fully already-realized result is positive, not NotEstablished.

The semantic obligation is to realize exactly the qualified UniqueCorrection against exactly the CandidateRevision within exactly the AcceptedRealizationScope without semantic expansion, unrelated work, or new product choice.
The prior RepairRealization must be positive and the prior RepairRealizationChallenge must target it and contain one or more objections.
The revision preserves exactly the same SurvivingMaterialBasis, AcceptedUniqueCorrection, AcceptedRealizationScope, CandidateRevision, and scoped CandidateView.
The revision cannot change the correction, expand scope, select another candidate, introduce a product decision, or perform a free second semantic search.
NotEstablished means only that the revision did not establish a valid repair realization and does not imply product underdetermination.
A positive revision requires one fresh RepairRealizationChallenge@1 and no second RepairRealization revision exists.
The challenged admission must contain a positive UniqueCorrectionCandidate.
Zero objections may derive AcceptedUniqueCorrection.
Objections to an initial candidate require the one UniqueCorrection revision when current and admissible.
Objections to a revised candidate establish the revised-challenge-objections UniqueCorrectionExhaustion branch.
UniqueCorrectionExhaustion never by itself means DECISION-REQUIRED.

The exact Discovery admission is the admission whose semantic result directly contains or produces the targeted statement, and the whole Discovery admission is retained in addition to the target Fact.
A positive candidate is the exact immutable UniqueCorrectionCandidate value: correction_requirements, derivation_claims, alternatives_considered, uniqueness_argument.
Every correction requirement is a semantic postcondition, never a file path, patch, implementation choice, or CandidateRevision-specific instruction.

A positive answer establishes that existing authority entails the correction, all requirements are supported, no required consequence is omitted, no unauthorized semantic effect or hidden assumption is introduced, and no materially distinct authority-compatible correction remains.
If a materially distinct authority-compatible correction remains, NotEstablished is required; NotEstablished does not imply DECISION-REQUIRED.
The prior UniqueCorrection must be a positive candidate and the prior UniqueCorrectionChallenge must target it and contain one or more objections.
The revision answers only those exact objections without changing the target statement or semantic family.
A revised candidate may cite exact prior challenge objections through their IDs.
NotEstablished terminates this bounded UniqueCorrection path.
A positive revision requires one fresh UniqueCorrectionChallenge@1 and no second UniqueCorrection revision exists.
